Cameron highlighting how early biomarker capture changes the adjuvant decision window in Lung Cancer ([3](#ref-3)). EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The most clinically significant finding at CTAD 2025 was the demonstration that Remternetug produced amyloid plaque clearance to <24.1 centiloids in 75.8% of participants at 12 months in the Alzheimer's Disease population studied by Randall Bateman and colleagues ([1](#ref-1)). In parallel, Eric Reiman presented data showing that the Plasma Abeta42/40 mass spectrometry platform delivered sensitivity 93.0% and specificity 90.0% for amyloid PET status across the validation cohort, reinforcing the role of this biomarker in patient stratification ([2](#ref-2)). The combination of these clinical and analytical signals was reflected in updated practice discussions, with Bart De Strooper highlighting how early biomarker capture changes the adjuvant decision window in Alzheimer's Disease ([3](#ref-3)). Across all plenary slots, the underlying message was that Alzheimer's Disease care is shifting from empiric to molecularly directed sequencing ([5](#ref-5)). Biomarker-driven recommendations expanded during the congress, with several sessions referencing the Plasma Abeta42/40 mass spectrometry performance characteristics — sensitivity 93.0% and specificity 90.0% for amyloid PET status — as the basis for incorporating the assay into routine practice ([2](#ref-2)). Speakers underlined that precision CV <8% across reference labs provides the analytical headroom needed to support guideline-grade adoption, with implications for both companion-diagnostic strategy and laboratory workflows ([4](#ref-4)). These positions were echoed in the implementation workshop, which catalogued the analytical and pre-analytical requirements for site adoption ([5](#ref-5)). On the competitive landscape, Remternetug was contrasted directly with donanemab in head-to-head and indirect-comparison datasets, with the new agent delivering amyloid plaque clearance to <24.1 centiloids in 75.8% of participants at 12 months ([4](#ref-4)). Eric Reiman positioned this as a competitive inflection for Alzheimer's Disease development, particularly for the cohort defined by the Plasma Abeta42/40 mass spectrometry ([2](#ref-2)). The platform discussion highlighted that Lilly's partnered-assay strategy now operates against a comparator field where precision CV <8% across reference labs is the new analytical benchmark ([4](#ref-4)). Real-world evidence presented in the late-breaking session further reinforced that early intensification under biomarker control improves outcomes ([3](#ref-3)). Looking forward, several presentations flagged ongoing unmet needs in Alzheimer's Disease, particularly around inter-laboratory reproducibility and the absence of standardised reporting templates ([5](#ref-5)). Various pointed to the need for prospective registry-based confirmation of the amyloid plaque clearance to <24.1 centiloids in 75.8% of participants at 12 months signal in routine practice ([4](#ref-4)). Forward-looking pipeline mentions included next-generation degraders and dual-mechanism platforms expected to enter pivotal evaluation within the coming year ([2](#ref-2)). The congress consensus indicated that next-generation platforms able to combine ultra-sensitive detection with broad mutation tracking will define the competitive ceiling over the coming cycle ([3](#ref-3)). --- ### 4.
